content.title: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Bitcoin ebook

The key to successfully selling digital products without relying on restricted platforms is to own your infrastructure. This means having full control over your online store, payment processing, and product delivery. With a sovereign digital commerce stack, you can accept bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, without having to worry about platform fees or restrictions. For example, NOWPayments charges only 0.5% per transaction, compared to Gumroad's 10% fee, which can save you $921 on 100 sales of a $97 product per month.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can start selling your digital products, you need to have a few things in place. First, you need to choose a hosting platform, such as GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, that can support your online store. You also need to select a backend logic platform, like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, to handle payment processing and product delivery. Additionally, you need to set up a storage solution, such as Supabase or Google Sheets, to store your orders and customer information.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To accept bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, you need to integrate a payment processor like NOWPayments into your online store. This involves setting up a payment gateway, configuring your store to accept cryptocurrency payments, and testing your payment pipeline to ensure it's working smoothly. You also need to set up an automated delivery system, using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, to deliver your digital products to customers instantly after payment confirmation.
Use a sovereign digital commerce stack to avoid platform fees and restrictions.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you can go live with your online store and start accepting bitcoin and other cryptocurrency payments. When a customer makes a purchase, the payment processor will verify the transaction and send a confirmation signal to your store, triggering the automated delivery of the digital product. With a sovereign digital commerce stack, you can process transactions quickly and securely, without having to rely on restricted platforms.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your online store grows and you start to receive more orders, you need to ensure that your infrastructure can scale to meet the demand. This involves monitoring your store's performance, optimizing your payment and delivery pipeline, and upgrading your hosting and storage solutions as needed. With a sovereign digital commerce stack, you have full control over your infrastructure, making it easier to scale and adapt to changing market conditions.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

To sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe, you can use a sovereign digital commerce stack that integrates a payment processor like NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and charges only 0.5% per transaction. This allows you to accept bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, without having to rely on restricted platforms, and gives you full control over your online store and payment processing.
Integrate NOWPayments to accept bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies.

If you're looking for a comprehensive solution to build, deploy, and scale a sovereign digital commerce stack, consider the Complete Builder Kit, available for $197 at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. This kit includes all 6 blueprints, plus all 7 templates, and provides everything you need to get started with selling digital products online, without relying on restricted platforms.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack, start by choosing a hosting platform and setting up your online store. Next, select a backend logic platform and integrate a payment processor like NOWPayments. Then, set up a storage solution to store your orders and customer information. After that, configure your store to accept cryptocurrency payments and test your payment pipeline. Finally, go live with your store and start accepting bitcoin and other cryptocurrency payments, and monitor your store's performance to ensure it's running smoothly.
